He basically says there is a scale from scalper to position trader with day trader and swing trader in between those. In the beginning, we are better at one extreme or the other. He suggests to look not at trading but at other areas of life on decision making. Do you make decisions quick? can shift mental gears in seconds? then probably you fit in really well in scalping and day trading. Another extreme is taking decisions slowly... When I thought about, it takes time for me to take a decision since I like to consider all options, outcomes and be ready. So by nature larger timeframes fit me better. Looking back at muy trading history all my good trades where on higher TFs. He mentioned as well goal should be to become well rounded trader in all aspects. But one has to become really good at something before taking another step. Ok. So figured this out. Next. Pitfall lies in when I analyze higher TFs and a a) I can't find setups for the near future so I go into lower timeframes.. and mess up usually. b) I need to define some zones on lower levels... after going a few timeframes down and marking what needs to marked... I get �stuck� there and start trading not just LTF but VLTF. So all of a sudden I went from Unconscious Unconsciousness wen to Conscious Unconsciousness. Baby steps I suppose. There is a book called Thinking Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman. Basically he describes that brain works in 2 modes: System 1 and System 2. System1 - intuitive (more efficient in the sense of energy required) and System 2 - rational, slow (not efficient, requires more energy). Our bodies are very very efficient so brain prefers to work in Mode 1(system) 24/7... It is a great challenge for most of people out there. Found a summary online by Eric Johnson. He labeled every certain heuristic so it is simple to follow. I can relate to pretty much every single heuristic he describes in terms of trading (and life). If you will read it... PLEASE READ IT SLOW! Re-read some parts if necessary. Read it twice... will read it few more times again. When I read I feel like someone picks my brain apart and points out where the errors come from. So I avoided losing 0,2R for 5R gain.. in risk terms, risk was 1 and potential gain 25. He rambles again.. shut up! There is a book called Thinking Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman. Basically he describes that brain works in 2 modes: System 1 and System 2. System1 - intuitive (more efficient in the sense of energy required) and System 2 - rational, slow (not efficient, requires more energy). Our bodies are very very efficient so brain prefers to work in Mode 1(system) 24/7... It is a great challenge for most of people out there. Found a summary online by Eric Johnson. He labeled every certain heuristic so it is simple to follow. I can relate to pretty much every single heuristic he describes in terms of trading (and life). If you will read it... PLEASE READ IT SLOW! Re-read some parts if necessary. Read it twice... will read it few more times again. When I read I feel like someone picks my brain apart and points out where the errors come from. Actually, when i zoom out the chart and look further to the left in H4 timeframe, i think the reason is not just only because the higher TF is calling for a impending downmove. I think my so-called blue flag limit may not be actually an important one because the resistance line you drawn may not really that important. Looking to the left, there is a supply right above them, which is then the important one. Price broke up from the compression and went all the way up, ignoring that supply which eventually becomes demand. Thus when price came down, it reacted to this supply-turned-demand zone and created the compression,making the bear flag. Subsequently, bear flag broke down successfully engulfed this demand and went straight to the next decision point aka my green flag limit which i think is the decision to engulf the supply and therefore price reacted to it. So I got this little tool (indicator developed) that helps me a lot every single day. Functions: Show spread: On/Off Color Font Extends rectangles: Extends rectangles to current bar Option to choose how many bars rectangle is extended into the future Option to show rectangle edge prices Show text (it will always be located in the middle of screen/box no matter TF for convenience). Choose text color Extends and straightens Trendlines: Extends AND straightens trendlines within deviation to current bar Option to choose how many bars rectangle is extended into the future Exception color (exception color trendline will be straightened out but NOT extended) Deviation (difference in percentage between Start Price to End Price. If above deviation then indicator will not adjust the TL hence you can draw trendlines with the same tool) https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2258-art?start=325 2/39 7/27/2018 ART - Page 14 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Usually deviation 0.3 or 0.4 % solves the issue of using trendlines as horizontal lines and as casual trendlines as well. So one can mark important areas and see the origin easily and still use trendlines to mark other important stuff since we don't use trendlines per say in this nice community What I do is create a template as you like, add indicator .. adjust all the settings. Then Save template as �Default� so next time you open any chart it has your layout + indicator set up and you can start doing your thing. Price broke up from the compression and went all the way up, ignoring that supply which eventually becomes demand. Thus when price came down, it reacted to this supply-turned-demand zone and created the compression,making the bear flag. Subsequently, bear flag broke down successfully engulfed this demand and went straight to the next decision point aka my green flag limit which i think is the decision to engulf the supply and therefore price reacted to it.
